title: Dhoni to Decide on IPL 2027 Before December, With Fitness Tests to Settle CSK Return
excerpt: The 45-year-old missed the entire IPL 2026 season with a calf injury. At a Bengaluru event he put the decision on his medical report, while CSK's chief executive said the call is Dhoni's alone.
body:
• MS Dhoni, 45, said at a healthcare event in Bengaluru on October 24 that he will decide before December whether he is fit to play one more IPL season for Chennai Super Kings in 2027.
  • Dhoni missed the entire IPL 2026 season with a calf injury, the first season since the league began in 2008 in which he did not play a single match.
  • He said the decision rests on medical test results, joking that doctors must keep "this old vintage vehicle running well on the road."
  • CSK chief executive Kasi Viswanathan said the call is Dhoni's alone; CSK, last champions in 2023, finished bottom in 2025 and eighth in 2026.

MS Dhoni will decide before December whether his body can carry one more Indian Premier League season. The 45-year-old former India captain, who missed the whole of IPL 2026 with a calf injury, said at a healthcare event in Bengaluru on Saturday that medical tests, not sentiment, will settle whether he returns for Chennai Super Kings in 2027.

"Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season," Dhoni said, in remarks recorded by ANI on October 24 and reported by The Sporting News and CricTracker.

"You will have to make sure that you do everything right with me and make sure that this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road. So all the pressure is on them."

— MS Dhoni, on his medical team

A season lost to the calf injury

Dhoni sat out the entire 2026 season with prolonged calf trouble. It was the first time since the IPL began in 2008 that he did not feature in a single match. He stayed with the CSK squad in a mentoring and strategic role, but the franchise missed the playoffs without him. His role had already narrowed before the injury: across IPL 2025 he batted in the closing overs as a finisher, scoring 196 runs in 13 innings at an average of 24.50 and a strike rate of 135.17.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PBDW5PKuz8s

Dhoni retired from international cricket in 2020, his last match for India the 2019 World Cup semi-final. That retirement later allowed CSK to retain him as an uncapped player ahead of the 2025 season. The question for 2027 is narrower than legacy: whether a 45-year-old wicketkeeper-batter can meet the physical demands of a full T20 campaign.

CSK's decision rests with one man

CSK chief executive Kasi Viswanathan has left the call entirely to Dhoni. "It's a question you need to ask him. I also have to ask him. He informs us of his decision when he arrives in Chennai. I have a feeling that the chances of him continuing to play for CSK are there. He is still a player, you know," Viswanathan said.

https://x.com/diganta_guha/status/2114051540763975952

The franchise around him is changing. Ruturaj Gaikwad has captained the side since 2024, and former India pacer Zaheer Khan has taken over as head coach following Stephen Fleming's departure. Results have dipped since Dhoni's last title as captain in 2023: CSK finished bottom of the table in 2025 and eighth in 2026, and have not advanced past the group stage since the captaincy handover.

What a return would mean

Dhoni remains the most successful captain in the franchise's history, leading CSK to five IPL titles, in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, and two Champions League T20 trophies. Even in a reduced finishing role, his presence changes how opponents bowl at the death and how CSK structure their batting order. For diaspora fans who plan travel and viewing around the IPL season, his decision, due before December, determines whether 2027 offers one more season of Dhoni in yellow or closes the playing career of the defining cricketer of the IPL era.

What happens next

The timeline is Dhoni's own: tests first, a report from his medical team, and a decision before December 2026. CSK's planning for the 2027 season, including retention and auction strategy, will be built around that answer. Until he gives it, the franchise and its supporters are in the position Viswanathan described: waiting to hear it from Dhoni himself.
